# VFD Pump Control Narrative Template

**Design rule:** The narrative describes behavior. Tags, ranges, engineering units, setpoints, delays and priorities stay in the I/O list and alarm database, and the narrative refers to them by tag or alarm ID. If a value appears in both places, the copies will eventually disagree, and commissioning will find out which one is wrong.

**Conventions:**
- `{{field}}` = fill in for this pump.
- `[N/A]` = section intentionally not applicable. Keep the heading so reviewers know it was considered.
- `[CONFIRM]` = an assumption that needs sign-off before FAT.

---

# Filled Example – P-1102

Anything you did not specify in the request is marked **[CONFIRM]**. I filled those items with typical choices so the example reads completely, but each one needs a project decision.

```
CONTROL NARRATIVE – VFD PUMP MODULE
Module tag:        P-1102
Description:       T-110 to T-120 Transfer Pump
P&ID:              [CONFIRM P&ID no.]
I/O list ref:      [CONFIRM doc no. / rev]
Alarm DB ref:      [CONFIRM doc no. / rev]
Module type std:   VFD-PUMP [CONFIRM library version]
Revision:          A – Issued for review
```

### 1. Function
P-1102 transfers product from mix tank T-110 to hold tank T-120. The batch system sets the pump speed. The pump is protected against running dry (low level in T-110), deadheading or line blockage (PT-1102), and overfilling the destination (high level in T-120).

### 2. Associated Equipment and Instruments

| Role | Tag | Signal type | Used for | I/O list row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Drive | VFD-1102 [CONFIRM tag] | [CONFIRM fieldbus / hardwired] | 4, 6, 7, 9 | per I/O list |
| Run feedback | VFD-1102 status word [CONFIRM] | Fieldbus | 9 | per I/O list |
| Suction (dry-run) protection | LSL-110 | DI | 5, 6, 10 | per I/O list |
| Discharge pressure | PT-1102 | AI | 6, 8, 10 | per I/O list |
| Destination overfill protection | LSH-120 | DI | 5, 6, 10 | per I/O list |
| Path valves | [CONFIRM: T-110 outlet / T-120 inlet valve tags, if automated] | DI/DO | 5 | per I/O list |
| Local disconnect | [CONFIRM: present? aux contact wired?] | DI | 6 | per I/O list |

### 3. Control Modes

| Mode | Start/stop | Speed source | Interlocks | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto (Batch) | Transfer phase on T-110 / T-120 unit | Batch phase speed parameter | All | Normal production mode |
| Manual | HMI faceplate | HMI speed setpoint | All | For draining and recovery |
| Local | [CONFIRM: drive keypad allowed?] | Drive keypad | Hardwired interlocks only | Maintenance only; HMI shows "LOCAL" |
| OOS | None | — | — | Removes the pump from batch availability |
| CIP | [CONFIRM: is P-1102 in the CIP circuit? If yes, define the LSL-110 handling during CIP. The tank may legitimately be near empty while flow is still needed.] | | | |

- **Auto → Manual:** The pump keeps running at its current speed (bumpless), and the batch system loses ownership of the pump. **[CONFIRM]**
- **Manual → Auto:** Allowed only when the pump is stopped. The batch system must acquire the pump. **[CONFIRM]**
- **Mode change:** Requires operator security level or higher. **[CONFIRM]**

### 4. Speed Control
- **Auto reference:** The batch transfer phase writes the speed reference in % of max speed **[CONFIRM: % vs Hz vs flow]**.
- **Manual reference:** HMI faceplate setpoint, in the same units.
- **Clamping:** The module clamps the reference to the min/max speed in the drive parameter list. Minimum speed is set to keep enough pump flow to avoid overheating. The value comes from pump data.
- **Ramps:** Ramp up and down are done in VFD-1102. Values are in the drive parameter file.
- **Bad or out-of-range reference in Auto:** The module holds the last good value, raises an alarm, and the batch phase goes to HOLD. **[CONFIRM]**
- **Closed-loop control:** None. Speed control only. If the transfer rate matters, the batch system calculates totals from T-110/T-120 level change.

### 5. Start Permissives

| # | Condition | Source | Modes | Operator message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Drive ready, no fault, communication healthy | VFD-1102 | Auto, Manual | "Drive not ready" |
| P2 | T-110 not low (LSL-110 healthy / not in alarm) | LSL-110 | Auto, Manual | "T-110 low level – dry run" |
| P3 | T-120 not high (LSH-120 not in alarm) | LSH-120 | Auto, Manual | "T-120 high level" |
| P4 | Transfer path lined up | Path valve feedbacks [CONFIRM] | Auto, Manual | "Path not lined up" |
| P5 | No latched P-1102 interlock awaiting reset | Module | Auto, Manual | "Reset required" |
| P6 | Not in OOS | Module | All | "Out of service" |

### 6. Interlocks (Trips While Running)

| # | Cause | Source | Action | Delay | Latch | Reset | Bypass | Class / Impl. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | T-110 low level (dry run) | LSL-110 | Ramp stop **[CONFIRM: ramp vs coast]** | per alarm DB (short debounce for sloshing / agitator surface) | Yes | Operator reset after LSL-110 clears | No **[CONFIRM: CIP exception]** | Equipment protection / PLC |
| I2 | T-120 high level (overfill) | LSH-120 | Stop | per alarm DB | Yes | Operator reset after LSH-120 clears | No | **[CONFIRM: process vs. safety.** If an overfill could cause a spill hazard or product loss above your tolerance, decide whether this must be hardwired into the drive enable or STO, independent of the PLC.**]** |
| I3 | Discharge pressure high-high (deadhead / blockage) | PT-1102, alarm DB ID per DB | Stop | per alarm DB | Yes | Operator reset | No | Equipment protection / PLC |
| I4 | Discharge pressure low-low while running (loss of prime / dry run backup) | PT-1102, alarm DB ID per DB | Stop | per alarm DB. Masked during the start ramp; mask time per alarm DB **[CONFIRM]** | Yes | Operator reset | Supervisor only, logged **[CONFIRM]** | Equipment protection / PLC. Backs up I1. |
| I5 | Drive fault | VFD-1102 | Drive trips itself; module goes to Faulted | — | Yes | Reset at HMI, which resets the drive fault | No | Drive internal |
| I6 | Local disconnect open | Aux contact [CONFIRM] | Module goes to Unavailable | — | No | Auto when closed. Pump does not restart; a new start command is required. | No | Hardwired |
| I7 | Drive communication loss | Bus diagnostic | Drive set to stop on communication loss (drive parameter) **[CONFIRM]** | per drive parameter | Yes | Operator reset | No | Drive + PLC |

**General rules:**
- After any interlock clears, the pump never restarts on its own. In Auto, the batch phase decides whether to re-command after the operator resets.
- Every interlock trip in Auto puts the transfer phase into **HOLD** **[CONFIRM: HOLD vs ABORT per interlock]**.

### 7. Start / Stop Sequence
- **Start:** The module checks P1–P6, enables the drive, and sends the speed reference. The drive ramps to the reference. Running is confirmed by drive feedback within the fail-to-start time. The PT-1102 low-low mask (I4) starts at the run command.
- **Normal stop:** Ramp stop **[CONFIRM]**. The batch phase closes the path valves only after run feedback drops, so the pump never deadheads against a closed valve.
- **Batch HOLD:** Pump stops; the phase holds ownership. **RESTART** re-checks permissives.
- **Batch ABORT / STOP:** Pump stops; ownership is released.

### 8. Alarms
Setpoints, delays and priorities are in the alarm database. Only module actions are listed here.

| Alarm DB ID | Condition | Module action |
|---|---|---|
| per DB | LSL-110 active | I1 trip, start permissive P2 |
| per DB | LSH-120 active | I2 trip, start permissive P3 |
| per DB | PT-1102 high (pre-alarm) | Annunciate only |
| per DB | PT-1102 high-high | I3 trip |
| per DB | PT-1102 low (pre-alarm, running only) | Annunciate only |
| per DB | PT-1102 low-low (running only, masked at start) | I4 trip |
| per DB | PT-1102 bad quality | See section 10 |
| per DB | P-1102 fail to start / fail to stop / uncommanded run | See section 9 |
| per DB | VFD-1102 fault / communication loss | I5 / I7 |

> PT-1102 low and low-low alarms must be suppressed while the pump is stopped. Otherwise they will stand permanently. Check that the alarm DB conditioning matches this.

### 9. Equipment Fault Handling

| Fault | Detection | Action | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fail to start | No run feedback within the timer after the start command | Remove the command, set Faulted, batch phase goes to HOLD | Operator |
| Fail to stop | Run feedback still present after the stop timer | Alarm. Command the drive to coast stop / disable. If still running, the operator must isolate locally. | Operator |
| Uncommanded run | Run feedback with no command (e.g. drive in Local) | Alarm. The module shows "Local" if the drive reports it. | Auto, when it clears |
| VFD fault | Drive fault bit | I5 | Operator |
| Communication loss | Bus diagnostic | I7. Drive stops on its communication-loss parameter. | Operator |

### 10. Instrument Failure Behavior

| Instrument | Failure detected as | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| LSL-110 | Wire break **[CONFIRM: is the switch wired fail-safe, i.e. de-energized = low? Is line monitoring available?]** | Treated as low. Pump trips (fail-safe). |
| LSH-120 | Wire break **[CONFIRM: fail-safe wiring, de-energized = high]** | Treated as high. Pump trips (fail-safe). |
| PT-1102 | Bad quality / out of range | Alarm. **[CONFIRM: stop the pump (conservative) or keep running on the LSL-110 / LSH-120 protection only, with the operator alerted. Recommended: stop in Auto; allow Manual run with a supervisor bypass.]** |

### 11. Power Loss and Restart
- **PLC restart:** All modules come up stopped and in their last mode. Latched interlocks stay latched. **[CONFIRM: retentive latches]**
- **Drive power return:** The drive does not auto-restart. Drive auto-restart / flying-restart parameters are disabled. **[CONFIRM]**
- **Batch system communication loss:** The pump keeps its current state and speed for a set time, then stops **[CONFIRM: time, or immediate stop]**. Alarm raised.

### 12. Batch System Interface

| Direction | Signal | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Batch → P-1102 | Acquire / Release | Ownership |
| Batch → P-1102 | Start / Stop command | |
| Batch → P-1102 | Speed reference | % of max **[CONFIRM]** |
| P-1102 → Batch | Running, At speed | At speed = feedback within a tolerance of the reference **[CONFIRM: tolerance from library default]** |
| P-1102 → Batch | Available (Auto, no fault, not OOS) | |
| P-1102 → Batch | Interlocked / Faulted + cause code | Cause codes from the library enumeration |
| P-1102 → Batch | Speed feedback | |

### 13. HMI
- **Faceplate:** Standard VFD-PUMP faceplate.
- **Displays:** Mode, state, speed reference and feedback, PT-1102 value, LSL-110 and LSH-120 states, active permissive and interlock text, bypass flag, owner (Batch / Operator).
- **Operator actions:** Start, stop, Manual speed setpoint, interlock reset.
- **Supervisor actions:** Mode change to OOS, I4 bypass (time-limited, logged) **[CONFIRM]**.

### 14. Test Notes
Standard VFD-PUMP module test, plus these P-1102-specific tests:
1. Simulate LSL-110 low while running. Pump stops, latches, and the phase goes to HOLD. Clear the switch and confirm no restart until reset.
2. Simulate LSH-120 high. Same checks as test 1. If I2 is hardwired, also prove it with the PLC in STOP.
3. Simulate PT-1102 high-high and low-low. Confirm I4 is masked during start.
4. Wire-break test on LSL-110, LSH-120 and PT-1102. Confirm the section 10 behavior.
5. Check the normal stop order: pump stops before the path valves close.

### 15. Open Items / Assumptions

| # | Item | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Is the LSH-120 overfill function process-only, or does it need hardwired / independent protection? | Process / safety | Open |
| 2 | Fail-safe wiring of LSL-110 and LSH-120 | Electrical | Open |
| 3 | PT-1102 bad-quality behavior | Process | Open |
| 4 | Is P-1102 in a CIP circuit? Dry-run handling during CIP | Process / QA | Open |
| 5 | Path valve tags and line-up permissive | Process | Open |
| 6 | Interlock → batch HOLD vs ABORT | Batch engineer | Open |
| 7 | Speed reference units | Batch engineer | Open |

---

### Suggestions for Rolling This Out Across 120 Modules
- **Make the library define the defaults.** Fail-to-start handling, communication loss and restart behavior should be specified once in a module-type standard. Each pump narrative then records only deviations, so sections 9 and 11 shrink to "per standard" for most pumps.
- **Generate sections 2 and 8.** Build the tag and alarm tables from the I/O list and alarm DB with a filter on module tag. Engineers should only write sections 1, 3–7, 10 and 15 by hand.
- **Keep the `[CONFIRM]` discipline.** Before FAT, no narrative should contain any open `[CONFIRM]` markers. That rule is easy to check by search.
